item.title: Retirement Age in America: The Surprising Truth Behind When Americans Actually Stop Working
item.description:
Americans are delaying retirement by four years on average as the cost of living continues to climb. Meanwhile, a growing number of workers are choosing to retire early rather than adapt to AI-driven workplaces. The question of when to retire has never been more complicated – or more consequential.

Key Takeaways:

  • The average American retires at 62, but full Social Security benefits don’t kick in until 67
  • Americans now say they need $1.46 million to retire comfortably
  • Rising costs are pushing expected retirement 4 years later than originally planned
  • Some workers are opting for early retirement rather than competing with AI

Retirement Age Is an “Ill-Defined Concept”

Ask five experts when Americans should retire, and you’ll get five different answers. That’s because, as Andrew Biggs, a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, put it: “There isn’t a retirement age. It’s not that there’s a retirement age sitting out there and we haven’t discovered it. It’s just that it’s an ill-defined concept.”

item.title: T. Rowe Price Shakes Up Investing With Crypto ETF and Credit Fund Launches
item.description:
A firm with 85 years of investment history is now betting on dogecoin, shiba inu, and 13 other digital assets — and that’s just the beginning of what T. Rowe Price has been up to this month.

Key Takeaways

  • T. Rowe Price filed an amended SEC registration for a 15-asset actively managed crypto ETF, one of the first of its kind in the U.S.
  • The firm launched OFLEX, a multi-strategy credit interval fund with Oak Hill Advisors covering both public and private credit markets.
  • T. Rowe Price expanded its global retirement leadership team with key new appointments to strengthen its retirement capabilities.
  • The firm manages over $1.6 trillion in assets as of December 31, 2025.

T. Rowe Price Crypto ETF: 15 Digital Assets Under Active Management

The Baltimore-based asset manager submitted an amended S-1 registration to the SEC in March 2026 for the Price Active Crypto ETF — a product that could become one of the first actively managed cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds in the United States.

item.title: Gen X Financial Reality: The $15 Trillion Generation Facing a Retirement Crisis
item.description:
Could the most powerful consumer generation in the world also be the least prepared for what comes next? Gen X — born between 1965 and 1980 — is quietly driving trillions in global spending, yet more than half doubt they’ll be financially ready when retirement arrives.

Key Takeaways

  • Gen X drives $15.2 trillion in global consumer spending, including $5 trillion in the U.S. alone
  • 54% of Gen Xers don’t believe they’ll be financially prepared for retirement
  • They think they need $1.57 million to retire comfortably — $310,000 above the national average
  • Nearly half (48%) expect to work during retirement, mostly out of necessity
  • Gen X spending power is projected to peak at $23 trillion globally by 2035

Gen X Spending Power Is Staggering — and Growing

Often dubbed the “forgotten generation” or the “middle child” sandwiched between Baby Boomers and Millennials, Gen X has been anything but invisible when it comes to economic impact. According to a joint report by NielsenIQ and World Data Lab titled “The X Factor: How Generation X is quietly driving trillions in consumer spending,” Gen Xers have been leading global consumer spending since 2021.
